red_flags: Did not move the case to provider selection despite a clear landlord approval
No acknowledgement sent to the landlord, unlike the human operator
Duplicate-ticket conclusion rests on matching job number and timestamp while the tenant and landlord contact IDs differ
reasoning: The landlord clearly approved ("yes please send someone"). The agent correctly read this and recorded the approval. The reference shows the human confirmed approval and moved the case to provider selection, assigning Stonebridge Works. The agent instead found ticket 90 with the same job number and a contractor already on it. It escalated to avoid double-dispatch and left the contractor assignment to the team. This is grounded in tool evidence and is cautious, with no invented facts and no landlord money committed. But the duplicate evidence was ambiguous, since the tenant and landlord contact IDs differ between the tickets. The case was not progressed on its own merits, and the agent added a human hand-off where the reference proceeded directly. Safe and reasonable, but it misses the expected outcome of moving to provider selection and sending a brief landlord reply.
